statement: Intel paused in 2024 and cancelled in 2025 because European greenfield capacity had become an option it could no longer fund, and unfunded sites ranked last under a cash-gated capital rule.
mechanism: The 2024 loss and the USD 10bn savings target broke Intel's capacity to carry new fixed commitments (FACT-005). Capital was therefore allocated by sunk-cost asymmetry: Arizona, Oregon, New Mexico and Ohio already had money in the ground and political weight, while Magdeburg had neither (FACT-001). Under that rule the European site is not rejected on merit but deferred indefinitely, because deferral costs almost nothing and commitment costs tens of billions. When a new CEO formalised the rule as 'capacity follows contracted demand' in 2025, the deferral became a cancellation (FACT-003). Weakest link: the assumption that Magdeburg carried no sunk cost of its own - if site preparation and supplier commitments were substantial, deferral was not cheap and the ranking logic weakens.

scope.where: Intel capital allocation across US, Ireland, Poland and Germany

relation_to_others.note: Both are necessary: no demand makes the option worthless, no cash makes it unaffordable
HYP-004 says the constraint was geographic, not fiscal; they predict different capex totals
Aid design raised the cost of deferral, reinforcing this mechanism
